welcome.intro: Point your Codex fleet at this router once and let it pool upstream accounts, keep session continuity, and record every call. Under two minutes of setup, one <0>config.json</0>, no secret in an env file.
welcome.storageText: A database — SQLite is the default and needs nothing but a writable directory.
welcome.upstreamText: Optional first upstream onboarding. API key can seed inline; browser OAuth, device OAuth, and imported auth.json hand off immediately after setup.
welcome.pluginsText: Initial intents for auth plugins — leaving them all off is a perfectly fine default in this build.

database.intro: Every routed request, every operator change, every upstream account lives in one OLTP engine. Pick it once; the schema is migratable, the engine choice isn't one-way.
database.dsnHintSqlite: File path, <0>file:</0> URI, or full driver DSN.
database.schemaMigrationHint: Applied automatically at boot. You can always re-apply from the CLI.

sqlite3.title: SQLite
sqlite3.pitch: One file on disk, no daemon, no credentials. Enabled with WAL + foreign keys out of the box. Best place to start.

postgres.title: PostgreSQL
postgres.pitch: Reuse your team's Postgres: backups, replication, observability. All migrations are idempotent and reviewable.

mysql.title: MySQL
mysql.pitch: DATETIME(6) for microsecond timestamps. Feature-parity with Postgres across migrations, pool, and indexes.

skipped.intro: You chose to skip upstream-account registration. The router will still migrate the database and write <0>config.json</0> on commit; you just have to add at least one account under <1>Admin → Accounts</1> before <2>/v1/*</2> traffic can land. That screen supports browser-OAuth, device-OAuth, and <3>auth.json</3> import onboarding.
skipped.body: Until an active account exists, every <0>/v1/*</0> call returns <1>503 no_available_account</1> and the admin dashboard flags the router as <2>degraded</2>. You can resume the flow at any time from Admin.

account.intro: The setup wizard and <0>Admin → Accounts</0> now expose the same four auth modes. API key can seed inline during commit; browser OAuth, device OAuth, and <1>auth.json</1> import continue immediately after setup lands.

methodDetails.api_key: Seeds the first upstream inline during setup. Fastest path to a ready router when you already have a key.
methodDetails.oauth_browser: Commit setup first, then continue immediately into the 003 browser sign-in flow under Admin -> Accounts.
methodDetails.oauth_device: Best for SSH or remote hosts. Setup commits first, then opens the device-code onboarding screen.
methodDetails.oauth_import: Finish setup, then land directly on the import screen to transplant an existing Codex CLI session.

form.providerHint: The setup seed stays OpenAI-only. Browser, device, and import still reuse the same provider after commit.
form.apiKeyHint: Stored verbatim (plaintext) in upstream_accounts in this build; encryption-at-rest arrives with the key-vault plugin in a later spec.
form.baseURLHint: Override for Azure OpenAI or compatible proxies. Leave empty for the default.

handoff.oauth_browser: Setup will finish first, then open the browser OAuth screen under Admin → Accounts so you can start the PKCE sign-in flow there.
handoff.oauth_device: Setup will finish first, then open the device-code screen under Admin → Accounts so you can approve from a second browser.
handoff.oauth_import: Setup will finish first, then open the import screen under Admin → Accounts so you can upload your local auth.json.
handoff.payloadBody: <0>first_account</0> is omitted for this mode. Setup still writes <1>config.json</1> and migrations first; account creation continues immediately after commit on the matching 003 route.

validation.nameMax: name must be at most 64 characters

pluginsStep.intro: Switching these on now records operator preference in <0>config.json</0>. If the matching plugin is not installed in this build, flipping the switch is intent-only and causes no behavioural change.

admin_auth.label: Admin authentication
admin_auth.description: Records whether admin sign-in should be enforced once that plugin is available. Today the admin API still uses the trusted-network boundary.

client_keys.label: Client API keys
client_keys.description: Records whether per-caller /v1/* keys should be enforced once that plugin is available.

review.introPrefix: Clicking commit runs the schema migration,
review.introSuffix: atomically writes config.json, and unlatches the setup gate. Takes a few seconds.
review.branchSkip: skips upstream-account seeding (add one in Admin → Accounts to unblock /v1/* traffic),
review.branchOAuthPrefix: finishes setup first, then hands you directly into the
review.deferredShort: — deferred · add in Admin → Accounts before /v1/* traffic
review.deferredContinue: — deferred · continue with {{method}} immediately after commit

noteImage.title: Shipping the same image twice?
noteImage.body: Set <0>ROUTER_DB_URL</0> before boot and the router skips this wizard entirely — same binary, different environments.

noteKeys.title: Keys never persist mid-wizard
noteKeys.body: Fields clear on refresh; DSN + API key only land on disk once you click <0>Commit and finish</0>.
